newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel wants clear rules for EMU stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Waigel wants clear rules for EMU stability pact.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said he would insist when meeting his EU colleagues in Dublin on Thursday that his proposed stability pact for the euro have clear penalties and verifiable definitions for exceptions.

According to his prepared text, Waigel told parliament the special ECOFIN session called before Friday's European Union summit still had to define when countries overshooting the Maastricht Treaty's deficit spending limits could be exempted from penalties.

Waigel also said Germany's overall public sector deficit from federal, state and local governments would be 2.5 percent of gross domestic product in 1997, the crucial year for qualifying for the single currency.

About the Dublin meeting, he said: "I will not move away from the clear stability goal. Every member state must know what the consequences are if it diverges from the stability path and lets its budget deficit go over three percent.
"The community procedure that then sets in must be transparent and unequivocal," he said, adding the pact needed "verifiable definitions" so it could be applied.
Waigel reiterated Bonn's opposition to loosening the criteria for entering the economic and monetary union as a way to boost employment.
